The hatchlings emerge as altricial nestlings, entirely dependent on parental provisioning for thermoregulation and food delivery during the critical early weeks of development. This initial egg mass is notably low compared to the adult body mass that the chick will eventually attain.

Adult female Bluish-fronted jacamars reach a maximum body mass of 25.3 grams [Wwi = 25.3 grams], a figure that aligns closely with the range of 22 to 26 grams reported for adults of this species in published field guides. This period of nest dependency is followed by a post-fledging phase during which the young bird gradually refines its foraging skills while still receiving occasional provisioning from the attending adults. The fledgling then enters a juvenile stage characterized by continued growth and feather maturation before attaining full independence.
